rationale: Both compile words to closures over a stack type. A is cleaner. A pop2 helper keeps the builtins short, the builtins live in a package-level map, and one resolve function handles numbers, user words and builtins identically at definition time. A definition state machine lets definitions appear anywhere in a line and catches unterminated ones. B's builtin switch repeats the same two-pop boilerplate for every operator. It only recognizes definitions when ':' is the first token of a line, and it silently defers unknown words in a definition to late binding at run time, which is inconsistent with its early binding of known words. A's push returning an always-nil error is a minor oddity, but overall it is more coherent and robust.
